description: Which authored block of a routine is open at this hour on this day, what goal that puts the NPC in pursuit of, what it is worth and where — plus the authored facts the KB carries and everything wrong with the authoring. US-1 of 125-npc-routines-and-locomotion.

cases.name: the-forge-shift-is-the-block-open-at-nine
cases.note: The ordinary case, and the one every other case is a departure from: one block’s window contains the hour, it names a goal and a place, and the whole output is one agent_goal/3 fact.

cases.name: market-day-outranks-the-shift-it-overlaps
cases.note: Two blocks open at once on the fifth day. The weekly exception is worth more, so it wins on priority — not on being authored later, which is what the reversed re-run proves.

cases.name: market-day-is-shut-on-a-day-that-is-not-market-day
cases.note: The same hour on the fourth day. A block that names days runs on those days only, so the shift is alone and the NPC is at the forge — the negative half of the case above.

cases.name: the-night-block-wraps-midnight-and-is-open-at-two
cases.note: endHour at or before startHour WRAPS, so the night is one block rather than two, and an implementation that compared start < hour < end finds nothing here.

cases.name: the-same-wrapping-block-is-open-at-twenty-three
cases.note: The other side of midnight, the same block. Two cases rather than one because a wrap is where an off-by-one lives, and each half fails independently.

cases.name: a-block-that-authored-no-priority-takes-the-world-default
cases.note: The night block authors none, so it is worth the world’s defaultPriority — which the graph facts also carry resolved, so a rule reading routine_block_priority/2 and core adopting the goal cannot disagree.

cases.name: the-gap-between-supper-and-the-night-block
cases.note: NEGATIVE. Nine in the evening: supper is over and the night has not begun. A gap is a real answer — the NPC holds no routine goal and does whatever else the world gave it, which is the difference between a routine and a scheduler that must always have one.

cases.name: the-gap-between-waking-and-the-shift
cases.note: NEGATIVE, and a second one on purpose: an implementation that special-cased the evening gap still fails the morning one. Nothing is due, nothing is adopted, and the delta is empty in both directions.

cases.name: two-blocks-at-one-priority-break-on-the-block-id
cases.note: The whole reason ties are specified. Two blocks of the watch are open at seven and both are worth thirty; drill wins because “drill” sorts before “stand_down”, and never because of where it sits in the authored list.

cases.name: a-block-with-no-place-wants-nothing-of-where-the-npc-is
cases.note: The watch at midnight names a goal and no location, so the destination is null and US-2 forms no movement intent. Somewhere to be is optional; something to want is not.

cases.name: a-window-whose-ends-coincide-is-the-whole-day
cases.note: Twenty-two to twenty-two. The degenerate wrap, and it is the whole day rather than nothing — which is how a routine with a single block is authored, and the case an implementation that treated start == end as an empty window fails.

cases.name: a-ten-day-week-puts-market-day-on-the-twenty-fifth
cases.note: The week length is AUTHORED. Day 25 of a ten-day week is weekday 5, so the market is open — and the same date in a seven-day week is weekday 4, which the next case pins.

cases.name: the-same-date-in-a-seven-day-week-is-an-ordinary-shift
cases.note: NEGATIVE for the case above: one authored number moves the whole calendar, and an engine with seven compiled in disagrees with the world it is running.

cases.name: a-goal-pursued-in-two-places-is-reported-rather-than-guessed-at
cases.note: NEGATIVE, of the authoring kind. A block’s place is a requirement of its GOAL, so one goal in two places can never be satisfied. The routine still resolves and still runs — a creator’s mistake is a report, not a crash — and issues names it, along with an hour no clock can match and a weekday outside the week. The block with no goal is DROPPED rather than defaulted, which is why resolved carries four blocks and not five.
